title: Self-neglect and missed care visits (synthetic)
setting: A social worker visits Keith Dawson, 64, at home at 27 Holloway Terrace, Harbridge, jointly with his district nurse after the nurse raised concerns about self-neglect and missed home-care visits.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Keith, it's Siobhan. I've brought Rachel, the social worker I mentioned.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, come in. Keep your coats on, mind.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Hi Keith, I'm Rachel. Thanks for letting me come. It's freezing out there today.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's freezing in here and all.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I can see. Is it okay if we sit in the front room?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Wherever. Move the papers.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thanks. So Siobhan asked me to come because she's a bit worried about how things are at home. I'll be writing notes. It's confidential, but if I think you're at risk I may need to share information, like with your GP. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: S'pose so.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Siobhan, you've been seeing Keith for his legs?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Yes, twice a week for leg ulcers, both legs. They're slow to heal.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Keith, tell me about the heating. It's very cold in here.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Boiler packed up. There's been no heating since October.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Since October? Have you got hot water?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: No. No heating, no hot water. I've got that little fan heater but it costs a fortune, so I don't put it on.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Is the house rented?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Housing association. I rang them once. Nobody came.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, we'll chase that. How are you managing with washing?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Not great. I, er. Well, without hot water.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: When did you last have a wash, roughly?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Honestly? I haven't washed in weeks. Three, four weeks maybe.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Thanks for being straight with me.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: It's not like I'm going anywhere.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And the kitchen, are you able to cook?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: There's rats in the kitchen. I've seen two. I don't go in there much now.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Rats in the kitchen. How long has that been?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Few weeks. They've been at the bread. I keep the food in here now, in tins.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. What are you eating day to day?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Soup, beans. Out the tin mostly. The carers were supposed to do me a meal.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Tell me about the carers. You've got a home care package?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Supposed to. Bright Days, they're called. Morning and teatime.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Can I come in on that? I've been looking at the log book in the folder by the door, the one the carers sign.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Please.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: In the last two weeks, there should have been 28 visits, and they've missed 16 of them. There's nothing written for 16 visits.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: 16 out of 28?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: Yes. And four days last week no one came at all. Keith told me he had no meal those days.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah. Nobody turned up. I didn't ring them, I didn't want the bother.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay, thank you, that's really helpful. I'll be contacting the agency about that today.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: There's one other thing, and I want to be careful. The neighbour at number twenty-five stopped me on the way in last week. She told me Keith has been drinking heavily.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Did you see anything yourself, Siobhan?

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: No, I haven't seen any sign of it myself. It's just what she told me.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. Keith, is there anything you want to say about that?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: She's a nosy cow. I'm not getting into it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Fair enough. Let's talk about your health generally. Who's your GP?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Dr Morgan at Holloway surgery. I've not been for ages.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And family, is there anyone around?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: My brother Phil, in Northby. We talk at Christmas. My wife left in 2015.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Okay. And money, what do you live on?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: ESA. And I'm waiting on the pension next year.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Are you up to date with bills?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I think so. The gas is on a meter.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: What would you like to happen, Keith?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: I just want the heating fixed. And the rats gone. I don't want a home or anything.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Nobody's talking about a home. You can stay here, but you need heat, hot water and the right support. Would you agree to me raising a safeguarding concern about the care visits and the state of the house?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: If it gets the boiler done. Yeah.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thank you. So, today I'll ring the housing association and log the boiler as an emergency repair. I'll ask for two oil heaters to be dropped off today or tomorrow.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll contact environmental health for pest control in the kitchen, and I'll raise the missed visits with Bright Days and our commissioning team today.

lines.speaker: S3
lines.text: I'll keep coming Tuesdays and Fridays for the legs, and I'll let you know if visits are still being missed.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: Thanks Siobhan. Keith, I'll also arrange a review of your care package and an occupational therapy assessment for the bathroom, so you can wash safely once there's hot water.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Okay. Would be nice to have a bath.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: And I'd like to ask Dr Morgan to see you. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Yeah, go on.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: I'll come back on Thursday the third of December, at two, to check the boiler's done and the agency's turning up. Here's my number if nobody comes.

lines.speaker: S2
lines.text: Cheers. Sorry about the state of it.

lines.speaker: S1
lines.text: No need to apologise. Stay warm, Keith.

disclosures.what: Keith says he has not washed in weeks, three or four weeks, because there is no hot water.
Keith says the boiler broke and he has had no heating and no hot water since October.
Keith says there are rats in the kitchen; he has seen two, for a few weeks.
Siobhan, the district nurse, says the home-care agency missed 16 of 28 visits in the last two weeks, including four days with no visit at all.
